findings.evidence: Independent groups: public contracts and schemas, then core logic, then callers, then tests and docs.
findings.fix: Cut this generic layering order, which the model already applies. Keep only the non-obvious rule that configuration or migrations come first when later behaviour needs them.

findings.evidence: Group files by purpose (not by directory), one group per reviewable idea.
findings.fix: Add a decision question for drawing group boundaries, for example: 'Before splitting, ask: can a reviewer verify this group without opening the other one? If not, merge. Does one rename touch many files? Make it one mechanical group, whatever the file count.'

findings.evidence: ## Gotchas lists git show <rev>:<path>, hunk headers, binary/submodule changes and generated churn, but has no item on large diffs being cut off silently
findings.fix: Add this gotcha: 'Harness tool output is truncated beyond roughly 10-30K characters without warning. Never build groups from a diff you did not see in full. Read `--stat`, then read the diff per path (`git diff <src> -- <path>`) so every file in the stat is actually read.'

findings.evidence: With no commits yet (`git rev-parse --verify --quiet HEAD` fails) there is no `HEAD` diff: collect both `git diff --cached --no-color` and `git diff --no-color` ... Nothing from either: report "No uncommitted changes to analyze" and stop.
findings.fix: Say whether the no-commit branch also runs the untracked-file step. As written, a fresh repo where every file is untracked reports 'No uncommitted changes'. Add: 'In both cases also include untracked files via `git diff --no-index`; report no changes only when all three sources are empty.'
